title: Attack optimality for three-round alternating two-key Even--Mansour
summary: Decide whether the three-round alternating two-key Even--Mansour construction admits an attack below the four-round data--time curve.

formal_statement.body: Let $N=2^n$ and let a three-round iterated Even--Mansour construction use two independent keys alternately, with round-key sequence $[K_0,K_1,K_0,K_1]$ and independent public permutations. In the source known-plaintext model, where preprocessing and online work are counted, does there exist an admissible asymptotic data regime $D\le N$ with a key-recovery attack of time strictly below $T(D)=N^2/D$ at equal data, up to polynomial factors in $n$? Alternatively, prove that $T(D)=N^2/D$ is a lower bound for this construction across the source data range.

scope.domain: Known-plaintext key-recovery attacks on three-round alternating two-key iterated Even--Mansour
assumptions: K0 and K1 are independent n-bit keys
The public round permutations are independent random permutations as in the source model
Preprocessing and online work count toward total time
Multiplicative polynomial factors in n are ignored
scope.unresolved_remainder: No inspected later work supplies a classical known-plaintext attack strictly below the source T(D)=N^2/D comparator for any admissible asymptotic data regime, nor a lower bound proving that comparator optimal for the full three-round alternating construction.

provenance.note: The first archived ePrint version received 2013-10-24 contains the fixed three-round alternating-key question and its four-round comparator.
